issues.translation_quote: Senior economist at the Fishery Design Institute
issues.justification: Expanding the Soviet acronym is acceptable, but it loses the bureaucratic-abbreviation flavor; minor expansion only. More serious: the name is invented rather than explained, flattening a period-specific institutional comic detail.

issues.translation_quote: Fris Street, Fish Street, - The Chikanuk pharmacy...
issues.justification: The spy's mangled phrase 'рыбна улица' is rendered as grammatical 'Fish Street', losing the foreign-accent/garbled-code feel.

issues.source_quote: Разрешите хотя бы… - Вот это попробуйте!
issues.translation_quote: - At least allow me to... - Now try this!
issues.justification: The colonel's reply refers to handing over a tool/item (a cigarette or drink); 'try this' is fine, but the earlier 'Не надо!' exchange comedic rhythm is flattened. Minor loss of the colonel's deadpan authority.

issues.source_quote: Их мама родила... Видно, в понедельник их мама родила
issues.translation_quote: Their mothers must have borne them on a Monday.
issues.justification: Stiff archaic 'borne' sits poorly with the light, comic children's-song register; also 'Ваши Mondays' rhyme and rhythm of the song are entirely lost, so the lyrics do not work as a singable comic song.
'Трын-трава' is a folk idiom (something of no consequence, 'who cares') tied to a magic herb; 'never-mind grass' is an invented calque that is opaque and the pun on 'всё равно/трын-трава' is lost.

issues.source_quote: Вам нужно обязательно встретиться с Вашим приятелем. ... скажете ему, что послезавтра с Вас снимут гипс.
issues.translation_quote: the day after tomorrow your cast comes off
issues.justification: Later dialogue states the cast comes off 'tomorrow'; the source itself is inconsistent but the translation also renders 'Завтра всё равно это снимут' consistently, producing a plot-logic contradiction left unaddressed.

issues.source_quote: Пока что - задаток. Мхяу-яу! Достаточно одной таблэтки...
issues.translation_quote: Just an advance for now. Mhyow-yow! One tablette is enough...
issues.justification: Playful deliberate mispronunciations ('таблэтки', 'туалэт', 'нумер') are rendered with random archaic/French-looking spellings ('tablette', 'toilette', 'feer tree'), which reads as typos rather than the villains' comic pseudo-sophisticated speech.

issues.source_quote: Кто возьмёт билетов пачку, тот получит... Водокачку!
issues.translation_quote: Whoever buys a whole stack of tickets wins... A water tower!
issues.justification: The rhyming couplet (пачку/водокачку) is lost; 'water tower' also misrenders водокачка (water pump house), and the joke of a ridiculous prize is without rhyme.

issues.source_quote: Шампанское по утрам пьют или аристократы, или дегенераты!
issues.translation_quote: Champagne in the morning is drunk only by aristocrats or degenerates!
issues.justification: Acceptable meaning, but 'Пьянству - бой!' rendered as 'War on drunkenness!' misses the Soviet slogan flavor; minor cultural loss.
Reference is to the 1961 currency reform (new money vs. old); 'New rubles' is ambiguous without context, though workable.
Fine in places, but Russian 'лопух' (gullible fool, also sucker) is rendered inconsistently as 'sucker' and elsewhere, slightly changing the nuance.

issues.source_quote: Билет... Дичь! ... Хм... Печёнкой чую, клюнула настоящая рыба.
issues.translation_quote: I can feel it in my gut, a real fish has bitten.
issues.justification: The fishing metaphor throughout is maintained, but 'клёв' wordplay in the 'fish will bite so well you forget everything' line is adequate; however 'Печёнкой' (liver) idiom is flattened to 'gut', minor loss.
The name play (Козадоев with козёл/'goat' undertones, Козлодоев as insult) is only transliterated; the English audience gets no sense that the boss is deliberately mangling the name as an insult.

issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты исдох! Чтоб я видел тебя у гробу, у белых тапках!
issues.translation_quote: May you drop dead! May I see you in a coffin, in white slippers!
issues.justification: The Odessan/Yiddish-inflected dialect of the curse (ungrammatical 'у гробу, у белых тапках') is lost; the curse is rendered in standard English, removing character voice and comedy.

issues.source_quote: Собака - друг человека! ... Управдом - друг человека!
issues.translation_quote: the building manager is man's best friend!
issues.justification: Works as a joke, but the earlier exchange 'Для эстетики' and the neighbors' comic bureaucratic voices become flat; acceptable but 'ЖЭК' rendered as 'housing office' is okay. Minor loss overall.

issues.source_quote: Упал, выругался... Чёрт возьми! Ух, прости, "Чёрт побери!"
issues.justification: The gag depends on two near-synonymous curses being the password; 'Damn'/'Damn it' are too close and the key password distinction ('возьми' vs 'побери') is lost, hurting the later password scenes.

issues.source_quote: Нет, я никуда не еду. Мы провожаем папу!!!
issues.justification: Speaker is a child/family member; 'Daddy' is fine, but the following 'Dun't' / 'tooreest' misspellings are odd stylization.
Artificial pun-like misspelling does not reproduce the Russian drunk/foreign mangling clearly.

issues.source_quote: Летять уткы… Летять у... утки... и-и два-а гуся-я...
issues.translation_quote: The duckies are flyin'... The du... ducks are flyin'... and-and two-o gee-eese...
issues.justification: Dialect dropping of g and 'duckies' do not correspond to the Russian dialectal spelling and add unwarranted cutesiness to a well-known song.
